findings.F1: The book's gain is the 14-day trend at Friday's close, not nearness to the yearly high: on all Fridays, the slope of the next-day excess return on the 14-day return is 0.0405 (t 3.35, 2136 cases, 366 days), while on every other weekday it lies between -0.012 and +0.014 (|t| ≤ 1.13), and over all days together it is 0.0023 (t 0.47).
findings.F2: Nearness to the yearly high adds little inside the regime: the tested slope has t 0.99, and the recomputed distance-below-high slope among up-trend Fridays is -0.0015 (t -0.06, 290 cases); the nearness quintiles of the cases run +0.40 %, +0.30 %, +1.02 %, +1.16 %, +1.16 % with t from 0.70 to 2.72.
findings.F3: The weekend move is all Saturday: after up-trend Fridays the Saturday-only excess is +0.69 % (t 3.19, 1055 cases, 281 days) against a two-day excess of +0.81 % (t 3.08), and the Sunday return's slope on the 14-day return is 0.0004 (t 0.04) against 0.0405 for Saturday. The book's mean daily return is +0.245 % on Saturday-dated days and +0.078 % on Sunday-dated days.
findings.F4: The grading by trend strength is monotone in its upper part: Friday two-day excess by 14-day-return quintile is -0.58 %, -0.59 %, +0.61 %, +0.54 %, +1.16 % (top quintile t 2.50). Down-trend Fridays give -0.35 % (t -1.20). The 7-day return grades less cleanly (top quintile +0.90 %, t 2.05; others between -0.29 % and +0.25 %).
findings.F5: The gain is not the market's own rise, one coin or a few trades. The market part of the book's mean bar gain is 0.0115 % of 0.0508 % (about 23 %). All six coins have positive case excess (+0.23 % BTC to +1.22 % XRP). The top 10 of 1777 trades carry 17.5 % of the summed net profit; 62 % of trades win, with a median of +0.67 %.
findings.F6: The gain is uneven over time but holds with one window left out (lowest Sharpe 0.999). Case excess is negative only in 2022 (-0.22 %, t -0.37) and near zero in 2023 (+0.10 %). It is strongest in 2020 (+1.49 %), 2024 (+1.54 %, t 2.53) and 2025 (+1.33 %, t 2.09). The book earned in up years and was flat in falling years (2018 mean -0.002 %/day, 2022 +0.001 %/day).

ideas.idea: The stronger a coin's 14-day return at its Friday close (UTC), the more it rises over the following Saturday (the next 24 hours), beyond its normal drift.
ideas.consequence: A trader would hold a Saturday long sized by the coin's two-week gain into Friday's close, and refuse the weekend long after a two-week fall.
ideas.name: Friday trend carries into Saturday

ideas.idea: Among coins that closed Friday (UTC) after a 14-day rise, the larger that rise, the more the coin rises over the next two days (Saturday and Sunday together), beyond its normal drift, whatever its distance from the yearly high.
ideas.consequence: A trader would size the weekend carry by the two-week trend rather than by nearness to the yearly high.
ideas.name: Weekend carry graded by trend
